newsitem.title: PERU: Amnesty worried by threat against Peru hostages.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty worried by threat against Peru hostages.

text.p: Amnesty International is "deeply concerned" by Marxist rebels' threats to execute hostages in the Peruvian embassy crisis unless the government accepted their demands, the human rights organisation said on Friday.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed their way into the Japanese ambassador's home on Tuesday during a diplomatic reception. Three days later, the rebels were still holding around 360 hostages, including at least eight ambassadors and top Peruvian government officials.
Amnesty said in a statement read aloud on radio here by a local sympathiser that it was "deeply concerned by the threat of the MRTA to kill hostages if the authorities do not accept its demands".

"Amnesty International calls on the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement MRTA to respect the security and integrity of the at least 200 hostages held in the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima," it added.

The London-based rights group said the MRTA had committed serious human rights violations since its inception in the early 1980s, such as the murder of civilians and the taking of hostages. It urged the rebels to respect and accept "without reservation" the rules of international humanitarian law.
